{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Solutions turned over 2026-09-02 for the cause in `fact:the-gap-replay-warning-exists-because-rehydrate-declines-to-run-when-the-caller-sent-text`.

THE SETTLED PART: `rehydrate_gaps` already resolves a gap by id against a live `detect_gaps()` and replaces the caller's copy wholesale. Its guard runs it ONLY when the caller sent an empty description and evidence. So the server has the authority and declines to use it in exactly the case where the caller's copy can be wrong. proj:chama's mangled title would have been repaired for free.

**THE QUESTION UNDERNEATH, which decides between every option below: is the pass-2 GapCandidate an INPUT the caller may legitimately shape, or an ECHO the server should treat as untrusted transport?** Nothing in the design says. The tool's own prose says "REPLAY EACH GAP OBJECT UNCHANGED", which reads as echo — but the code's behaviour is input.

OPTIONS, none preferred:

· **A — Always rehydrate.** Resolve every gap by id, replace wholesale, delete the guard. Kills the class outright and the ⚠ warning becomes unnecessary. Cost: one `detect_gaps()` per serve pass, already batched to once per call. ⚠️ REAL BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: a gap that has CLOSED since the caller's copy was taken currently gets served; after this it refuses with `gap_is_gone`. Whether refusing is correct is a judgement nobody has been asked for — recording a Question against a gap that no longer exists is arguably worse than refusing, but it is a change consumers would feel.

· **B — Rehydrate, fall back to the caller's copy when the id does not resolve.** Kills the mangling class and keeps today's tolerance for closed gaps. ⚠️ Its weakness is silence: a caller who edited the text deliberately loses the edit with no signal, and the two cases (mangled / closed) become indistinguishable in the reply.

· **C — Verify rather than replace: compare the caller's copy to the server's, refuse on mismatch and name the difference.** Turns a silent degradation into a loud refusal, which is the shape this project already prefers elsewhere — `create_edges` is all-or-nothing, and `gaps_to_prompts` refuses a MIXED batch rather than half-serving it. Costs the caller a round trip. ⚠️ It also treats every difference as an error, which is only right if the answer to the input/echo question is "echo".

· **D — Accept `gap_id` as chama asked, and deprecate the object form.** Their literal request. On its own it is a patch: the old path stays and stays trusting. As a DEPRECATION it is different — new callers take the safe door, the old one warns, and it is removed later, which is `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` clause two rather than a workaround.

· **E — Do nothing; the warning is already there.** ⚠️ Recorded because it must be argued against rather than skipped, and the argument is short: the warning is loud, specific, correctly placed, and it still did not work. A field report from a first session hit the failure anyway.

⭐ WHAT MAKES A AND C DIFFERENT IN KIND, not just in cost: A says the server owns the text and quietly makes it right. C says the caller asserted something false and must be told. Both are defensible; they answer the input/echo question opposite ways, and choosing a mechanism without answering it first is how this guard got its current condition in the first place.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — on gap_to_prompt's second pass, is the GapCandidate the caller's INPUT or the server's ECHO? The whole repair follows from that and nobody has stated it","rationale":"Recorded as an idea rather than repaired directly because the cheapest-looking fix (A, delete the guard) carries a consumer-visible behaviour change that nobody has approved, and because the reporter's own request (D) is the one option that is a patch unless it is paired with a deprecation.

⚠️ The bound on all of this: the guard's current condition is not obviously WRONG — it was written for budgeted replies and does that job correctly. What is missing is a statement of what the second pass's argument is FOR, which would make one of these options obviously right and the rest obviously wrong.","status":"proposed"}
